work_order.understanding: ReportCard, the shared wrapper all 17 dashboard cards render inside, wraps its content in a <Button variant="bare"> whenever the card has a `to` route and is not in edit mode (ReportCard.tsx:108-127). The component library's Button renders react-aria-components' Button and forwards only className, so it always emits a literal <button>. Any widget body containing its own button nests <button> inside <button>. CalendarCard's per-month Button (CalendarCard.tsx:443) is the only body that does so today — I re-grepped all 17 callers — so it is the card React names, but the fault is the wrapper, not CalendarCard. /reports/custom and /reports/spending never mount ReportCard, which is why they are clean. Fix at the shared layer so every widget is corrected at once (IAC-4). I reproduced the nesting and validated the proposed replacement and its tests by running them, not by reading them.
work_order.root_cause: ReportCard renders its children inside a literal <Button> as the card's click target. The component library's Button wraps react-aria-components' Button and offers no element override, so it always emits a <button>. Any dashboard widget body containing a button produces invalid <button>-inside-<button> DOM. The wrapper is the fault: the same nesting would appear in any widget rendering a control, and ReportCard is the single shared layer all 17 cards pass through.
work_order.approach: Replace the <Button variant="bare"> wrapping `content` in ReportCard's clickable branch with a <View role="button" tabIndex={0}> carrying onClick and an Enter/Space onKeyDown — the idiom already used by CleanupListRow, TypePicker and EmptyState in this repo. This removes the <button> element from the card's own markup so descendants may legally contain buttons, correcting every card through one shared change. Deliberately do NOT add aria-label: a role="button" element still derives its accessible name from its contents, which keeps the e2e page model's name-based selectors matching — verified by test. Carry over height/width 100%, textAlign left and overflow visible, and add cursor: pointer (the old Button got it from its &[data-hovered] rule). Keep the Button import — Layout's edit-mode menu still uses it. Add a unit test rendering ReportCard with a button child, asserting the DOM contains no `button button` and that React logs no nesting warning. Keep AC-5 as a browser capture-and-compare gate, NOT a test gate: the previous plan was rejected for claiming VRT baselines proved the layout when the command it named cannot compare a pixel, so the layout check is stated as what it is.

files.change: In the `if (to && !isEditing && !disableClick)` branch (lines 108-127), hoist `const goToReport = () => navigate(to, { state: { goBack: true } });` above the return, then replace the <Button variant="bare" onPress={...}>{content}</Button> with a <View role="button" tabIndex={0} onClick={goToReport} onKeyDown={e => { if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ') { e.preventDefault(); goToReport(); } }} style={{ height: '100%', width: '100%', textAlign: 'left', overflow: 'visible', cursor: 'pointer' }}>{content}</View>. Add a comment stating why this is deliberately not a Button. Do not add aria-label. Leave the non-clickable branch, Layout, and the edit-mode menu Button untouched; keep the Button import, which Layout still needs.

work_order.debate_summary:
There was no critique to judge: plan/critique.json is an empty object, so the council produced one position and no rebuttal. That is a gap in the council, not a reason to rubber-stamp the proposal — so I treated the proposal as unverified and re-derived it from the code myself.

Everything load-bearing in it survives. I reproduced the nesting by running a test rather than reading one: `button button` count 1, React's validateDOMNesting pair captured, card tagName BUTTON. I applied the proposed fix to a scratch copy and re-ran: count 0, zero console messages, tagName DIV, and navigate called exactly once with the right arguments for click, Enter and Space. I independently re-grepped the 17 ReportCard callers and confirmed CalendarCard is the only body rendering a button, confirmed the three repo precedents for the role="button" idiom, and confirmed the component library's Button has no element override. I also confirmed the last rejection's technical claim in full: fixtures.ts:53-62 short-circuits to a synthetic pass whenever VRT is unset, the plain `playwright` script does not set it, and .sdlc/config.yml:172 has verify.e2e empty. The proposal's answer to that rejection — reclassify AC-5 from verify:"test" to verify:"browser" with a concrete capture-and-compare, and demote VRT to an explicitly-optional step that says what it cannot prove — is the right one, and it is the main reason this plan should not be rejected a second time for the same reason.

Where I depart from the proposal is by adding to it, in three places, all found by reading code the proposal did not read.

First, and most concretely: the proposal enumerated which of the old Button's layout properties are dropped (flex row/center, borderRadius, WebkitAppRegion) and argued each is inert. That argument is right. But the old Button also set color: theme.buttonBareText, fontSize 13 via styles.smallText, a hover background-color and an active background-color — and the proposal's style carry-over list mentions none of them. Most are genuinely inert: the sole child carries explicit width/height 100%, the card body paints its own opaque background over the button's, and 'no-drag' only bites beneath a 'drag' ancestor, of which FinancesApp has exactly one. But colour and font-size are inherited properties, and the replacement View sets neither, so the card body now inherits both from FinancesApp's root View and the html/body default instead of from the Button. In light and dark those resolve to the same values. I did not read midnight.css or palette.css line by line, so I cannot promise that. That is a new acceptance criterion (AC-6) and an added theme sweep in the QA script, not a change to the approach.

Second: the card's onKeyDown now sits on an ancestor of the inner button, where before a native button intercepted it. The proposal tested that clicking the inner control does not activate the card but did not test Enter on it. I probed it — navigate stayed at zero, because react-aria's inner Button stops propagation — but that is a property of the inner control, not of ReportCard, and it would regress silently if the inner control changed. It is now a seventh test case and a QA step.

Third: I checked the proposal's claim that the VRT baselines need the pinned container over HTTPS, and it holds — bin/run-vrt sets E2E_START_URL to https://localhost:3001 and playwright.config.ts:20 reads baseURL from it. So the optional VRT step is honest about why it may diff for unrelated reasons.

The honest disagreement is about confidence, not about the plan. I set 80, two below the proposal's 82, and the reason is specific: the proposal's residual risk list is organised around layout, which is right, but it treats the dropped Button properties as a closed question once the layout ones are argued away. They are not closed, because two of the dropped properties are inherited rather than geometric, and one of them has a theme-dependent answer I did not verify. Two more acceptance criteria and two more QA steps is what that costs, and it is cheaper than discovering a midnight-theme text-colour shift after merge.

I did not seek any change to the route. debug → implement → review → qa is right: debug was needed to pin down that the fault is the shared wrapper rather than CalendarCard, implement changes one production file, review is where the div-with-button-role trade and the dropped-style carry-over deserve a second opinion, and qa is the only stage that can actually see the console warning and the pixel delta. Nothing I found needs a stage the route lacks.

`packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/ReportCard.tsx:124`

Evidence: Probe H: native <button type="button" onClick={inner}> inside a clickable ReportCard, focused, then fireEvent.keyDown(btn,{key:'Enter'}) followed by the fireEvent.click(btn) a browser synthesises on Enter. review.title: A's finding 0 is real but its stated severity understates the second half of the failure: the missing target guard does not merely double-navigate, it makes the descendant control keyboard-dead. The card's handler calls e.preventDefault() on a keydown it should have ignored, and in a real browser preventing default on a native button's Enter keydown suppresses the browser-synthesized click entirely. So the outcome for a native <button> descendant is 'card navigates, inner control does nothing' — the inner control loses its keyboard activation altogether — not 'both handlers run'.

Evidence: ReportCard.test.tsx:32-62 defines takeRecords() (54), root (58), rootMargin (59), scrollMargin (60) and thresholds (61). validated_work_order.understanding:
Two things were wrong with the revision that came back from the plan reviewer, and one of them is a factual error that would have shipped a regression to all twelve report routes.

OBJECTION 1 (the useDashboardWidget predicate) is correct and I measured it. I ran react-query v5 in jsdom and recorded all four states: disabled+no data {pending, idle, isPending TRUE, isLoading false}; enabled first fetch {pending, fetching, true, true}; resolved {success, idle, false, false}; cached background refetch {success, fetching, isPending FALSE, isLoading false, isFetching TRUE}. The rejected revision reported isPending/isLoading as `query.fetchStatus !== 'idle'` and claimed in both `approach` and `risks` that the change was confined to the loading branch. The fourth row refutes that: fetchStatus is 'fetching' during a background refetch over cached data, so that predicate is true while the data is present and correct — every report route would blank to <LoadingIndicator /> and unmount its subtree on every dashboard-to-report navigation and every window refocus. Corrected to `const isFirstLoad = query.isPending && query.fetchStatus !== 'idle'`, which changes exactly one of the four states (row 1, isPending true → false) and leaves the other three untouched.

OBJECTION 2 (AC-2 vs AC-8) is also correct: AC-2 demanded /reports/spending 'behave exactly as today', which on the base commit means spinning forever, while AC-8 requires it to render. AC-2 is rewritten in place to its real intent ('the nesting fix must not disturb these routes') and now names AC-8 as governing their loading behaviour; AC-8 is not weakened. The reviewer also asked for AC-2's before/after in plan/ac-diff.md — that file is generated by .sdlc/bin/plan-strategy.mjs from the ledger's validated_ac_changes, which post-work-order.mjs populates by diffing this acceptance[] against the posted one, so recording it is a consequence of making the change, not a separate edit.

What survives unchanged, because 15 of 18 QA checks prove it: the v1 diagnosis. ReportCard wrapped every widget body in a literal <button>; the shared-wrapper fix is right and stays.

What the rejected revision also got factually wrong: its recorded reason for not using usePress ("did not fire at all for Enter or for mouse down/up on a div in this environment"). I re-ran that probe and it does not reproduce — usePress on a div here fires for Enter, Space and mouse, once each, and suppresses repeats. The DECISION not to switch still stands, on timing and coverage instead: usePress moves activation to its own model (Space commits on keyup, Enter on keydown), QA's T-8 and T-17 both measure that timing, there is no browser here to verify against, and 15 passing checks depend on the current model. The alternative's recorded reason is rewritten to the one I actually acted on.

BUG-002 is covered by AC-7 (added in the rejected revision, kept unchanged) — duplicating it would buy QA a second browser run and no coverage. BUG-001 gets a new criterion, AC-9, so the finding QA actually made has a criterion addressed to it.
validated_work_order.root_cause: Three separate causes. (1) ReportCard's click surface was rebuilt by hand — the previous attempt replaced react-aria's <Button> with a View plus a hand-written onKeyDown and carried over only the Button's geometry, dropping the press semantics the primitive owned. usePress suppresses key auto-repeat; this handler does not, so one Space press plus auto-repeats navigates once per repeat (T-17: 6 navigations). (2) AC-5 asserted that the old card showed a hover background. It never did: the Button's inline `background: transparent` outranks its own `&[data-hovered]` background-color rule in the cascade, and the opaque card body painted over the wrapper regardless, so the card's painted background has always been the card surface colour at rest and on hover (T-12 measured a property the product never had). (3) /reports/spending with no widget id spins forever because useDashboardWidget enables its query with `!!id && !!type` and a disabled react-query v5 query stays status 'pending' forever, while every report component returns <LoadingIndicator /> while pending. Pre-existing on main and untouched by PR #26, but the route must load, so it is fixed here — in the shared hook, by reporting isPending/isLoading from `query.isPending && query.fetchStatus !== 'idle'` so only a first load reads as loading and neither a disabled query nor a cached background refetch does. The rejected revision's fetchStatus-only predicate was also true during a background refetch over cached data and would have blanked all twelve report routes on every navigation and refocus; that is corrected.
validated_work_order.approach: Keep the div-based click surface that fixes the nesting (15 of 18 checks depend on it) and change three things; everything else in the rejected revision is kept. A: restore the press semantics explicitly and testably in ReportCard's keydown handler — return early on `e.repeat`, return early when `e.target !== e.currentTarget`, keep `e.preventDefault()` ahead of both so holding Space cannot scroll, keep activating on keydown for Enter and Space so T-7/T-8 do not change. Do not switch to usePress: the rejected revision's stated reason for rejecting it does not reproduce, but the decision stands on timing and coverage grounds (usePress commits Space on keyup, T-8 and T-17 both measure that timing, no browser here to verify the swap, 15 passing checks depend on the present model). B: leave the card's appearance exactly as it is — add no hover background; the card has never painted one and adding it is the appearance change this issue rules out of scope. C: fix the loading state narrowly in the shared hook — `const isFirstLoad = query.isPending && query.fetchStatus !== 'idle'`, returning `{ ...query, isPending: isFirstLoad, isLoading: isFirstLoad }`, which is react-query's own isLoading definition and changes exactly one of the four query states (a disabled query, isPending true → false). All twelve call sites destructure { data, isPending } or { data, isLoading } and already handle `widget === undefined`, so no report component changes.

risks: The corrected predicate is confined to one state of one query, and that confinement is the point. `query.isPending && query.fetchStatus !== 'idle'` is true only for an enabled query whose first fetch is in flight with no cached data. Measured against react-query v5 in this repo it changes exactly one of four states: disabled + no data goes from isPending true to false (the T-5 fix). Enabled first fetch with no data stays true; enabled and resolved stays false; enabled with cached data undergoing a background refetch was already false and stays false, because isPending derives from status and a successful status persists through a refetch. Nothing reaches a route that has a widget id and is not mid-refetch, and nothing outside the loading branch of any of the twelve call sites changes.

The `e.target !== e.currentTarget` guard suppresses a card activation when a key event originates from a descendant. That is the intent, but if a future widget renders a focusable child that relied on bubbling to open the card, Enter on it would stop working — the month-name checks (T-9, T-10) will catch that.

Changing useDashboardWidget touches twelve report components at once. They all destructure { data, isPending } or { data, isLoading } and all already handle widget === undefined, so the change reaches the loading branch only; the new hook test asserts all four query states directly, including that a cached background refetch never puts a loading indicator on screen.

The AC-5 and AC-9 corrections rest on the cascade: an inline `background: transparent` outranks the Button's `&[data-hovered]` background-color rule, so the tint never painted.
